what: ## DCC2. To codegen-rq-mir-constcheck: what `note_trait_if_possible` reads, for a call that is not const What: for `NonConstClosure`, `NonConstOperator` and `NonConstDerefCoercion` with `conditionally: false`, rustc's `FnCallNonConst` runs `note_trait_if_possible(err, self_ty, trait)` (`check_consts/ops.rs`): - `self_ty` a type parameter: `suggest_constraining_type_param` of `[const] {trait_ref}` on the caller's generics; - `self_ty` an ADT whose selected impl (`SelectionContext::select` of the trait ref, `ImplSource::UserDefined`) is not `const`: the span note "impl defined here, but it is not `const`" at the impl's `def_span`. Wanted: on those three kinds, `self_ty: StoredTy` (the call's `args.type_at(0)`), the trait ref's args (`StoredGenericArgs`, for printing `[const] Trait<..>`), and `non_const_impl: Option` (the selected user impl when it is not a `const impl`). `NonConstOperator` already has `trait_`; the closure's trait is its `Fn*` trait, the deref's `Deref`. Why: these are rustc's notes on every such error; the lowering has no solver to select the impl.
